directAnswer: To reset a pull request, you can revert the changes in your branch and then push the updated branch to the remote repository.
summary: Resetting a pull request involves reverting changes or resetting the branch to a previous commit. This process may vary slightly depending on the version control system you are using.

sections.heading: Using Git
sections.body: To reset a pull request in Git, you can use the 'git reset' command to move your branch pointer to a specific commit.

sections.heading: Steps for GitHub
sections.body: Follow these steps to reset your pull request on GitHub.

steps.title: Identify the commit
steps.detail: Find the commit hash you want to reset to by using 'git log'.

steps.title: Reset your branch
steps.detail: Run 'git reset --hard <commit-hash>' to reset your branch to that commit.

steps.title: Force push changes
steps.detail: Use 'git push origin <branch-name> --force' to update the remote branch.

steps.title: Check the pull request
steps.detail: Go to your pull request on GitHub to ensure it reflects the reset state.

faqs.question: What happens to my changes after a reset?
faqs.answer: After a hard reset, all changes made after the specified commit will be lost unless they are saved elsewhere.

faqs.question: Can I reset a pull request in other platforms?
faqs.answer: Yes, the process is similar in other platforms like GitLab or Bitbucket, but the UI and commands may vary.

faqs.question: Is it safe to force push?
faqs.answer: Force pushing can overwrite changes in the remote branch, so ensure that no one else is working on the same branch.

caveats: Force pushing can lead to loss of data if not used carefully.
Ensure all collaborators are aware of the reset to avoid confusion.
